result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right and recommend a separate favicon mark and an embroidery version. B covers more of the causes: thin strokes, tiny text, small gaps closing up, low-contrast colors and gradients, plus specific mm minimums and a ready-to-send designer brief. Both suggest checking at actual size and getting a sew-out, but neither suggests the quick one-flat-color check. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is only partly right and blame a logo that was never adapted for small or stitched use. Both recommend separate favicon and embroidery versions, a sew-out proof and a real-size check. A edges ahead because it names more causes (gaps closing from fabric pull, low-contrast colors going gray, light and dark tab backgrounds) and plainly says this is a small, cheap job. B's deference to the shop's own minimums and its one-page vendor spec are good touches, but its account of the causes is a little thinner.
